scenes.tts: Remove one wing bud from a chick embryo. The neurons serving that limb come out fewer. Were they never made? Or were they made, and then lost?
scenes.visual: Title card: Too Small, or Lost? A three-day chick embryo outline with one wing bud fading out. Two question marks: never made? made, then lost?
scenes.narration: Remove one wing bud from a chick embryo. The neurons serving that limb come out fewer. Were they never made? Or were they made, and then lost?

scenes.tts: First, two words. A target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with, such as a limb muscle or a gland.
scenes.visual: An axon grows from a neuron to a limb muscle and a gland; the muscle and gland glow, labelled target.
scenes.narration: First, two words. A target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with, such as a limb muscle or a gland.

scenes.tts: A ganglion is a cluster of neuron cell bodies outside the brain and spinal cord.
scenes.visual: A cross-section of the spinal cord with a cluster of cell bodies beside it, labelled ganglion, outside the cord.
scenes.narration: A ganglion is a cluster of neuron cell bodies outside the brain and spinal cord.

scenes.tts: Spinal ganglia sit beside the cord and hold sensory neurons. Sympathetic ganglia hold neurons of the sympathetic nervous system.
scenes.visual: Two labelled clusters: spinal ganglion (sensory neurons) beside the cord; sympathetic ganglion in a chain nearby.
scenes.narration: Spinal ganglia sit beside the cord and hold sensory neurons. Sympathetic ganglia hold neurons of the sympathetic nervous system.

scenes.tts: In nineteen thirty-four, Viktor Hamburger removed one wing bud from chick embryos about three days old.
scenes.caption: In 1934, Viktor Hamburger removed one wing bud from chick embryos about three days old.
scenes.visual: Schematic chick embryo, about three days old. A wing bud on one side is removed; the other side is marked comparison. Credit: Hamburger, 1934.
scenes.narration: In 1934, Viktor Hamburger removed one wing bud from chick embryos about three days old.

scenes.tts: On the operated side, the neurons serving that limb came out reduced.
scenes.visual: Two spinal ganglia side by side, later in development: the operated side smaller. Label: schematic, not to scale.
scenes.narration: On the operated side, the neurons serving that limb came out reduced.

scenes.tts: Hamburger first read this as the limb controlling how many cells grew in the spinal cord and its ganglia.
scenes.visual: An arrow from limb to spinal cord and ganglia labelled: limb controls how many cells grow? (first reading, 1934).
scenes.narration: Hamburger first read this as the limb controlling how many cells grew in the spinal cord and its ganglia.

scenes.tts: But one count at the end hides a choice. A small ganglion has two possible histories.
scenes.visual: The small ganglion with a single count stamp. Two faint paths branch backward in time from it.
scenes.narration: But one count at the end hides a choice. A small ganglion has two possible histories.

scenes.tts: Predict. What are the two histories? And what would you measure to tell them apart?
scenes.visual: Question card over the two branching paths: what are the two histories, and what would you measure?
scenes.narration: Predict. What are the two histories? And what would you measure to tell them apart?

scenes.tts: Fewer neurons might have been made. Or the normal number might have been made, and then lost.
scenes.visual: Path one: a few neurons appear and stay. Path two: many neurons appear, then several fade out. Both end at the same small ganglion.
scenes.narration: Fewer neurons might have been made. Or the normal number might have been made, and then lost.

scenes.tts: Both give a small ganglion at the end. To separate them, you count at a series of stages.
scenes.visual: A time strip with counts taken at successive stages, ticks along a time axis.
scenes.narration: Both give a small ganglion at the end. To separate them, you count at a series of stages.

scenes.tts: You also mark the cells that are dividing, and the cells that are dying.
scenes.visual: On the time strip, dividing cells marked with one symbol and dying cells as dark dots.
scenes.narration: You also mark the cells that are dividing, and the cells that are dying.

scenes.tts: In nineteen forty-nine, Hamburger and Rita Levi-Montalcini did exactly that, in chick spinal ganglia.
scenes.caption: In 1949, Hamburger and Rita Levi-Montalcini did exactly that, in chick spinal ganglia.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Hamburger and Levi-Montalcini, 1949, chick spinal ganglia.
scenes.narration: In 1949, Hamburger and Rita Levi-Montalcini did exactly that, in chick spinal ganglia.

scenes.tts: They followed the ganglia stage by stage, after removing or adding limb tissue.
scenes.visual: The time strip animates stage by stage for operated and control sides.
scenes.narration: They followed the ganglia stage by stage, after removing or adding limb tissue.

scenes.tts: Many neurons formed and grew fibres before the deficit appeared.
scenes.visual: Early stages: operated and control ganglia look alike; neurons sprout fibres on both sides.
scenes.narration: Many neurons formed and grew fibres before the deficit appeared.

scenes.tts: Degenerating cells became conspicuous later.
scenes.visual: Later stages: dark dots, dying cells, appear in the operated ganglion; its size falls behind.
scenes.narration: Degenerating cells became conspicuous later.

scenes.tts: The neurons had been made. Then they were lost.
scenes.visual: Caption on screen: made, then lost.
scenes.narration: The neurons had been made. Then they were lost.

scenes.tts: So the limb seemed to keep neurons alive. It was not only calling them into existence.
scenes.visual: The limb outline linked to the ganglion by an arrow labelled: helps keep neurons alive?
scenes.narration: So the limb seemed to keep neurons alive. It was not only calling them into existence.

scenes.tts: Three conclusions follow. First, neurons are made in excess, and then lost.
scenes.visual: A list builds on screen. Item 1: made in excess, then lost.
scenes.narration: Three conclusions follow. First, neurons are made in excess, and then lost.

scenes.tts: Second, whether they are kept depends on the target.
scenes.visual: Item 2: kept or not depends on the target.
scenes.narration: Second, whether they are kept depends on the target.

scenes.tts: Third, the target must supply something neurons need. If it supplies too little for all of them, they must in effect compete.
scenes.visual: Item 3: the target supplies something; too little for all means competition.
scenes.narration: Third, the target must supply something neurons need. If it supplies too little for all of them, they must in effect compete.

scenes.tts: Neither the something nor the competition had been shown. They were inferences.
scenes.visual: Items 3 marked with a dashed outline and the word: inferred, not yet shown.
scenes.narration: Neither the something nor the competition had been shown. They were inferences.

scenes.tts: The neurotrophic hypothesis would have to earn them, one test at a time.
scenes.visual: Title: the neurotrophic hypothesis, with an empty checklist beside it.
scenes.narration: The neurotrophic hypothesis would have to earn them, one test at a time.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea to carry through. Make too many, then let the target keep what it can feed.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: Make too many, then let the target keep what it can feed.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea to carry through. Make too many, then let the target keep what it can feed.

scenes.tts: The test case is nerve growth factor, N G F. Acting as a survival factor, it decides how many neurons made stay alive.
scenes.caption: The test case is nerve growth factor, NGF. Acting as a survival factor, it decides how many neurons made stay alive.
scenes.visual: The card adds: nerve growth factor (NGF); acting as a survival factor, it decides how many of the neurons made stay alive.
scenes.narration: The test case is nerve growth factor, NGF. Acting as a survival factor, it decides how many neurons made stay alive.

scenes.tts: It can never raise that number above the number made.
scenes.visual: The card adds: never above the number made.
scenes.narration: It can never raise that number above the number made.

scenes.tts: So a small ganglion is a question about history. Count across time before you decide.
scenes.visual: Closing card: one count gives a size; counts across time give a history.
scenes.narration: So a small ganglion is a question about history. Count across time before you decide.
